slides.title: VoiceGuard: An Audio-Native LLM-VLA Pipeline for Wheelchair-Mounted Assistive Manipulation
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates an audio-native pipeline combining LLMs and Vision-Language-Action models to enable natural language control of wheelchair-mounted robotic arms, addressing challenges in command disambiguation and safe interruption.

card.one_liner: VoiceGuard enables safe, voice-controlled wheelchair-mounted robotic manipulation via validated LLM routing and local stop mechanisms.
card.key_idea: Audio-native LLM routes speech to structured packets; rule-based dispatcher validates before SmolVLA execution; on-device stop bypasses cloud.
card.evaluation: Preliminary tests: 55/60 routing, 16/20 deliveries, 20/20 stops (210ms latency). Limited by lab setting and single author trials.
card.limitation: VLA execution sensitive to lighting/background; requires network for routing; not yet validated with actual wheelchair users.

slides.title: WiTac: Wrist-Informed Tactile Representations for Contact-Rich Manipulation
slides.tldr: FUSING WRIST VISION WITH TACTILE SIGNALS
slides.highlight: Integrating wrist vision with tactile signals before policy injection significantly improves contact-rich manipulation success rates compared to vision-only or wrist-free tactile approaches.

card.one_liner: Fusing tactile signals with wrist vision before policy injection improves contact-rich manipulation success rates.
card.key_idea: Pretrained encoder fusing tactile histories, kinematics, and wrist views into contact tokens via cross-attention, conditioning VLA policies.
card.evaluation: Real-world tests on Sharpa North robot across four tasks; boosted GR00T and pi-0.5 success by 28.8% and 15.0% over baselines.
card.limitation: Lacks depth-based 3D alignment, ignores joint temporal evolution of vision/touch, and limited to one robot platform and four tasks.

slides.title: Physics-Informed Tactile-based Shape Estimation of Deformable Linear Objects
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates that dense tactile sensing combined with a physics-informed Vision Transformer can accurately estimate the 3D shape of deformable linear objects without visual input, offering a robust alternative for manipulation in occluded environments.

card.one_liner: Tactile-only ViT framework estimates 3D deformable object shapes without vision using physics-informed losses.
card.key_idea: Fuses Sparsh tactile features and proprioception via cross-attention, regressing B-spline control points with Discrete Elastic Rods loss.
card.evaluation: Validated on steel/USB cables via RMSE/Chamfer metrics; outperforms pose-only and ResNet baselines; generalizes with minimal fine-tuning.
card.limitation: Requires two grippers and quasi-static motion; inference latency (61.5ms) may limit high-speed control loops.

slides.title: TaF-Foundation: Wrench-Grounded Cross-Sensor Tactile Representations
slides.highlight: This work establishes a unified tactile representation space by grounding heterogeneous sensor data in six-dimensional wrenches, enabling effective cross-sensor transfer and improved manipulation performance.

card.one_liner: Wrench-grounded tactile representations enable cross-sensor transfer and improved robotic manipulation.
card.key_idea: Grounds tactile features in 6D wrenches via shared encoder and sensor-specific adapters, trained on 100M paired observations.
card.evaluation: Tested on 24 sensors for wrench estimation, retrieval, and manipulation; outperforms baselines in RMSE and success rates.
card.limitation: Adapting to unseen sensors requires labeled tactile-wrench pairs and training sensor-specific modules, limiting zero-shot deployment.

slides.title: Objectives as Policies: Vision-Language Model Cost Programs for Contact-Rich Manipulation
slides.tldr: VLM-GENERATED COST PROGRAMS FOR MPC-BASED MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework that bridges vision-language models and model-predictive control by generating editable objective programs for contact-rich manipulation, enabling iterative refinement via simulation before real-world deployment.

card.one_liner: VLMs generate editable objective programs for MPC, enabling zero-shot contact-rich manipulation via digital twin refinement.
card.key_idea: A pretrained VLM creates multi-stage cost programs from a library, iteratively refined via simulated MPC rollouts in a digital twin.
card.evaluation: Tested on four tabletop tasks; 97.5% sim success, 80% real-world. Outperforms L2R, ReKep, CoRAL, and VLAs.
card.limitation: Relies on accurate digital twin physics; fails with grasp slips due to friction estimation errors and rigid-body assumptions.

slides.title: From Human Videos to Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation Data: Confidence-Guided RL Refinement of Video Priors
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework that converts human video priors into executable robot demonstrations by using reinforcement learning to refine motion estimates, addressing embodiment gaps and uncertainty in bimanual dexterous manipulation.

card.one_liner: PriDex converts human videos into bimanual robot data via confidence-guided RL refinement of motion priors.
card.key_idea: Preserves interaction structure by using affordance-based grasps and confidence-adaptive RL to balance object and wrist motion priors.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on four EgoDex tasks in Isaac Sim; outperforms H2S2R and ViViDex baselines in simulation and distilled policy success.
card.limitation: Requires high-quality video reconstruction; wrist guidance may hinder tasks where simplified motions are more stable than demonstrated ones.

slides.title: NF-VLA: A Normalizing-Flow Baseline for Vision-Language-Action Learning
slides.tldr: AUTOREGRESSIVE NORMALIZING FLOWS FOR VLA CONTROL
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates that autoregressive normalizing flows, trained via a single maximum-likelihood objective, can achieve competitive performance in vision-language-action tasks, offering a unified framework for policy training, action generation, and refinement.

card.one_liner: NF-VLA uses autoregressive normalizing flows with score-based refinement to achieve competitive vision-language-action manipulation.
card.key_idea: Combines conditional autoregressive normalizing flows with a deep-shallow architecture, trained via exact maximum likelihood on Gaussian-smoothed actions.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on LIBERO (98.35% success) and LIBERO-Plus (72.6%), outperforming baselines like π0.5 and OpenVLA-OFT.
card.limitation: Relies on Gaussian smoothing and a single score-based correction step, which may limit robustness under severe distribution shifts.

slides.title: Right Goal, Wrong Body: Re-grounding Frozen VLAs under Actuation Shift
slides.highlight: This work introduces ReGround, an inference-time method that restores performance of frozen Vision-Language-Action models under actuation shifts by re-grounding intended motions using motor babbling, achieving near-oracle success rates without retraining.

card.one_liner: ReGround restores frozen VLA performance under actuation shift by re-grounding intended motion via learned dynamics.
card.key_idea: Inference-time method using motor babbling to learn deployed dynamics, tracking intended trajectories with trust-region MPC, and activating only upon shift detection.
card.evaluation: Tested on two VLAs across eight LIBERO tasks with five shift settings; restores near-oracle success (e.g., 0.90 at 400ms latency) and reduces unsafe episodes.
card.limitation: Requires initial motor babbling for dynamics identification; effectiveness depends on accurate shift detection and may struggle with highly non-linear or unmodeled dynamics.
